cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Outdo the Effort
cards.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put a cross beside my name after bringing me dinner. I've put two beside yours; I'll cook for you twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That cross means delivered, not owed. I've brought tomorrow's dinner too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delivered, yes. I'll put four ready-made meals on your doorstep. Then you can mark them straight off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm away all week. Just wash the dishes; I'll collect them when I'm back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the return collection. Leave me your keys and I'll wash everything in your kitchen while you're away.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 mistakes delivery marks as debts and doubles them; A3 doubles actual meals and A5 exceeds B requested dish washing.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 extra dinner leads A3 four meals; B4 absence and dishes redirect A5 to the whole kitchen.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers care and B4 limits repayment to an ordinary small chore.

heightening.evidence: A5 exploits B4 absence to propose a much larger service, asking for keys.

specificity.evidence: A1 names and deliveries establish a food-care arrangement without specifying a rota location.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 return collection is an awkward detachable prefatory phrase; key request itself is direct.
